newsitem.title: FINLAND: HUHTAMAKI CEO SEES UPWARD PROFIT TREND.
newsitem.headline: HUHTAMAKI CEO SEES UPWARD PROFIT TREND.

text.p: Finnish confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki Oy's CEO Timo Peltola said in the 1996 annual report received on Wednesday that Huhtamaki was a reborn company with an upward profit trend.
"In essence, Huhtamaki is a reborn company, with a clear mission and strategy for the coming years, and an upward profit trend reinstated," Peltola wrote in the report.

The group's agenda was short, but not necessarily simple, he said, adding: "to invest the proceeds from disposals sensibly, to help Leaf and Polarcup achieve their strategic objectives without compromising Huhtamaki's financial imperatives."
Leaf is Huhtamaki's confectionery division and Polarcup its packaging business.
In 1996, Huhtamaki sold its Leiras and Star pharmaceuticals units and the Donruss collectible cards business. It also agreed on an asset swap with Hershey Foods of the United States.

The restructuring had "radically changed Huhtamaki's shape," Peltola said, noting three billion markka worth of annual sales had been divested while acquisitions would boost sales by 0.8 billion markka. In 1996, net sales were 7.5 billion markka.
"Royalty and rental income associated with the divestments will generate substantial income in the coming years," he said.
"Our balance sheet is very strong and permits major moves to improve the market positions of Leaf and Polarcup, Peltola said, but did not elaborate.
In 1996, Huhtamaki's profit after financial items rose 33 percent to 416 million markka and EPS rose 36 percent to 10.29 markka.

The annual report repeated an earlier forecast by the company that: "after a weaker relative performance early in the year, a further improvement in full-year earnings per share can be expected." --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
